subject: Access history and export spec — follow-up from discovery call
messages:
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>
To: Emily Chen <emily.chen@paybridge.com>
Cc: Raj Patel <raj.patel@paybridge.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 20 Jun 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Access history and export spec — follow-up from discovery call

Hi Emily / Raj,

Thanks again for taking the time earlier today — appreciated the clear framing of PayBridge's compliance needs. Quick recap and next steps from our side so we stay aligned on the audit/logging capabilities you asked about: 

Key asks you raised on the call:
- Full chronological access history for customer data (who, what, when) for the last 24 months, exportable on-demand.
- Ability to filter logs by internal user id, API key, model id and dataset id.
- CSV or JSONL export that preserves UTC timestamps and includes request/response metadata (token counts redacted), plus a checksum.
- SLA for producing exports (preferred: within 48 hours for ad-hoc exports; weekly automated exports to S3 for longer retention).

What I promised to send now:
1) A short spec for the export format we think will meet those needs (attached: redwood-audit-format-spec.pdf).
2) A small sample extract from our dev environment to confirm the fields/shape (attached: sample_access_log.csv).
3) Intro to our security lead (cc'd below) to handle evidence requests and any PII redaction/segregation questions.

Next steps / asks for you:
- Can you confirm the minimum time window you need standard (e.g., 24 months vs 36 months)?
- Any particular columns required in the export (e.g., IP, region, user role, justification tag)?
- Preferred delivery mechanism for exports: S3 push, secure portal download, or encrypted email?

I'll let Rishi take the more technical evidence questions in the reply — copying Sean so he can continue the procurement thread for pricing impacts of longer retention.

Best,
Vanessa Ortiz
Account Executive — Redwood Inference
vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0124

Attachments: redwood-audit-format-spec.pdf (12KB), sample_access_log.csv (8KB)
From: Emily Chen <emily.chen@paybridge.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>
Cc: Raj Patel <raj.patel@paybridge.com>
Date: Mon, 22 Jun 2026 08:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Access history and export spec — follow-up from discovery call

Hi Vanessa,

Thanks for the recap — that matches our needs. A few clarifications from the compliance team before we loop external auditors: 

1) Retention window: we require 36 months of immutable access logs, with the ability to run targeted extracts going back the full period.
2) Required fields: user email, internal employee id, service/component (e.g., inference-gateway), model id, dataset id (if applicable), action (read/write/export), resource id, UTC timestamp, request-id, and a minimal response status (success/fail). IP is optional but preferred.
3) PII: PayBridge will mark certain customer fields as regulated — we need redactions on export or a column-level mask flag to indicate redacted values.
4) Export format/delivery: prefer S3 push with server-side encryption (AES256) to a bucket we manage; as a fallback secure portal download is acceptable.

For the audit evidence we might ask for:
- A sample of recent ad-hoc export you can produce within 48 hours, with both CSV and JSONL formats.
- A description of how you guarantee immutability (append-only storage, WORM, or signed checksums).
- If possible, a hashed mapping of internal employee ids so we can map accesses without sharing raw PII.

Can Rishi or someone from security confirm whether the sample export will include request/response metadata or if those fields are redacted by default?

Thanks,
Emily Chen
Head of Compliance — PayBridge Payments
emily.chen@paybridge.com
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Emily Chen <emily.chen@paybridge.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>
Cc: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 22 Jun 2026 08:42:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Access history and export spec — follow-up from discovery call

Hi Emily — thanks for the clear list. I'm Rishi, security and compliance at Redwood — looping in the technical details below and answering your questions.

Short answers to your points:
- Retention: Redwood supports configurable retention policies. For hosted accounts we can retain immutable access logs for 36 months (append-only store backed by WORM-enabled buckets) under an enterprise agreement.
- Fields: The sample CSV attached mirrors almost exactly the schema you requested; we include: utc_timestamp, request_id, internal_user_id (hashed by default), user_email (redacted by default on exports), component, model_id, dataset_id, action, resource_id, response_status, ip_address, org_id, and checksum.
- Redaction & mapping: By default exports redact PII fields (user_email) and provide a hashed_user_id column. If PayBridge needs the reversible mapping, we can arrange a secure tokenization key exchange under a DPA addendum, but that requires an approval workflow and audited key access.
- Export delivery: We can push encrypted exports (CSV and JSONL) to your S3 with server-side encryption (AES256) and signed URLs for downloads. Exports are produced as gzipped CSV/JSONL and include a SHA256 checksum file.
- SLA: For ad-hoc exports, SLA is 72 hours for standard requests and 48 hours under an expedited 24/7 agreement. Weekly automated exports are configurable.

Attached is a tiny sample (sample_access_log.csv) from a dev tenant — headers included at top. Example header row: utc_timestamp,request_id,internal_user_id,user_email,component,model_id,dataset_id,action,resource_id,response_status,ip_address,org_id,checksum

Notes about immutability: we store logs in an append-only pipeline with Kafka topic retention piped into S3 with object-lock enabled (WORM). Checksums are computed and stored in a separate metadata store; we can provide signed checksum manifests for auditor verification.

If you'd like, we can produce a 48-hour ad-hoc export for a 30-day window as a proof-of-concept pushed to your S3 test bucket. I'll need: target S3 bucket ARN, IAM principal for uploads, and scope of data (org_id / dataset_ids).

Let me know what works and we can set the action items.

-Rishi
Rishi Malhotra
Security & Compliance — Redwood Inference
rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai

Attachments: sample_access_log.csv (8KB), redwood-audit-format-spec.pdf (12KB)
From: Emily Chen <emily.chen@paybridge.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 22 Jun 2026 09:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Access history and export spec — follow-up from discovery call

Thanks Rishi — this is exactly the level of detail we needed.

We can proceed with a 48-hour PoC export for a 30-day window. I'll open a short-lived S3 bucket for the push and share the ARN + upload principal with you by EOD. Please redact user_email by default and include hashed_user_id; we'll request reversible mapping only if auditors need it.

Action items agreed:
- PayBridge (Emily) to share S3 ARN and IAM principal by EOD.
- Redwood (Rishi) to schedule PoC export within 48 hours of receiving access details (CSV + JSONL, gzipped, with SHA256 manifest).
- Redwood (Vanessa) to provide draft DPA addendum language about temporary tokenization key if reversible mapping is requested later.

Emily
